sentences.text:
Author: N.Tukaramji
Bench: N.Tukaramji
 The Honourable Sri Justice N.Tukaramji
 I.A.Nos. 2 And 3 Of 2025
 In/And
 Criminal Petition No. 5396 Of 2025
Common Order

This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS, 2023'), seeking quashment of the proceedings against the petitioners in Crime No. 198 of 2024 of Langerhouz Police Station, Hyderabad.

2. The petitioners are arrayed as accused Nos.1 to 7 in the Crime registered for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 498-A, 406, 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 and Sections 3(1)(w)(i), 3(1)(w)(ii), 3(1)(r)(s)(c) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention Of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2015.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention Of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2015
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. Heard Mr.S.Someshwar Rao, learned counsel for the petitioners, Mr.Jithender Rao Veeramalla,
learned Additional Public Prosecutor, representing the respondent No.1-State and Mr.K.Narain Chakravarthy, learned counsel for respondent No.2/de-facto complainant.

4. Pending this petition, the parties have entered into the compromise and, accordingly, they moved I.A.Nos.2 and 3 of 2025 with the prayer to permit them to enter into compromise and by recording the settlement to 2 NTR,J I.A.Nos.2 and 3 of 2025 in/and quash the proceedings against the petitioners/accused Nos.1 to 7 in Crime No. 198 of 2024.
5.
This Court vide order dated 21.04.2025 referred the parties to the High Court Legal Services Committee for identification and to verify the voluntariness in arriving the settlement.

The Secretary, High Court Legal Services Committee, has submitted report dated 02.05.2025 stating that the parties were identified by their respective counsel and also on verification of Aadhar Cards/Identity Cards and the enquiries revealed that the parties have willfully and without coercion entered into settlement/compromise.
6. I have considered the submissions of the learned counsel and perused the materials on record.

7. Having considered the allegations, the charged offences, which are essentially matrimonial and inter-personal in nature and taking into account the amicable settlement between the parties and to restore peace among them, in the light of the dictums in Gian Singh v. State of Punjab and another 1 and Anil Mishra v. State of U.P. 2; State of Madhya Pradesh v. Laxmi Narayan and others 3, this Manikanta Patwari vs The State Of Telangana on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110636193/

entities.text: Manikanta Patwari vs The State Of Telangana

sentences.text:
1 Court is of the considered view that quashment of the impugned proceedings in view of 2012 (10)
SCC 303 2024 INSC 189 2019 (5) SCC 688 3 NTR,J I.A.Nos.2 and 3 of 2025 in/and the settlement by exercising jurisdiction under Section 482 Cr.P.C./528 of BNSS, 2023, would be in the interest of justice.
8.
Accordingly, I.A.Nos.2 and 3 of 2025 are allowed.

Consequently, all proceedings in Crime No. 198 of 2024 of Langerhouz Police Station, Hyderabad, are hereby quashed against the petitioners/accused Nos. 1 to 7.
9.
In the above terms, the Criminal Petition is disposed of.
Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.

_ _ ________ N.TUKARAMJI, J Date: 09.06.2025 svl Manikanta Patwari vs The State Of Telangana on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110636193/
